content.title: Emergency Preparedness
content.summary: Emergency preparedness is essential for ensuring personal safety during disasters, and individuals are encouraged to develop their own response plans. Key actions include staying informed through local alerts, creating a family communication plan, and assembling an emergency kit with essentials to sustain oneself for at least 72 hours. The city also promotes resources like the Inside Arvada podcast for further education on emergency preparedness.

## Emergency preparedness starts with you

Personal preparedness is the best way to ensure your safety during any type of emergency or unexpected shock. We encourage every person to develop a plan for responding to disasters.

### Take these actions to be prepared

1. [Be Informed](#tab7a57c257-a0c5-477f-915f-50ec5b3d7b6c_0)
2. [Make a Plan](#tab7a57c257-a0c5-477f-915f-50ec5b3d7b6c_1)
3. [Build a Kit](#tab7a57c257-a0c5-477f-915f-50ec5b3d7b6c_2)

1. [Be Informed](#tab7a57c257-a0c5-477f-915f-50ec5b3d7b6c_0)

**[![decorative](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6317)](https://www.smart911.com/smart911/ref/reg.action?pa=LookoutAlert)**

When emergencies happen, getting accurate information quickly is critical.

- Sign up for [**LookoutAlert**](https://www.smart911.com/smart911/ref/reg.action?pa=LookoutAlert) — the fastest way to get local evacuation notices, weather alerts, and safety updates.
- Follow official City channels on [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/cityofarvada/), [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/cityofarvada/), [X (Twitter)](https://twitter.com/cityofarvada), and [Nextdoor](https://nextdoor.com/agency/city-of-arvada/?i=rzqtffymdcqgzrmlqqbd).
- Bookmark trusted sources: [FEMA](https://www.fema.gov/), [Ready.gov](https://www.ready.gov/), [National Weather Service Boulder,](https://www.weather.gov/bou/) [Jefferson County Public Health](https://www.jeffco.us/4872/Public-Health).
- Keep a [**NOAA Weather Radio**](https://www.weather.gov/bou/nwrnoaa) on hand (tune to 162.550 MHz for Jefferson County).

1. [Make a Plan](#tab7a57c257-a0c5-477f-915f-50ec5b3d7b6c_1)

**![decorative](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6319)**

A little planning now can save precious minutes later.

- Know the**ways out** of your neighborhood.
- Choose a **family meeting place** if you’re separated.
- Create a **communication plan** — pick one out-of-area friend or family member everyone can contact.
- Plan for pets — have carriers, leashes, and food ready.
- Visit [Ready.gov/plan](https://www.ready.gov/plan) to get started.

1. [Build a Kit](#tab7a57c257-a0c5-477f-915f-50ec5b3d7b6c_2)

**![decorative](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6318)**

Emergencies may last several days — prepare to be self-sufficient for at least **72 hours**.

**Essentials:**

- Water (1 gallon per person per day)
- Non-perishable food
- Flashlight and extra batteries
- First aid kit and prescriptions
- Important documents in a waterproof bag
- Phone chargers and power banks
- Blankets or sleeping bags
- Cash in small bills

**Tip:** Customize for children, older adults, medical needs, and pets. Visit [Ready.gov](//Ready.gov) for special needs considerations.

## Prepare for Local Hazards

Arvada is exposed to a variety of hazards — here’s how to be ready:

1. [Wildfire](#tab4614c9c6-6538-492c-b047-782cf8690dbc_0)
2. [Flood](#tab4614c9c6-6538-492c-b047-782cf8690dbc_1)

1. [Wildfire](#tab4614c9c6-6538-492c-b047-782cf8690dbc_0)

**![wildfire](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6320)**

### Preparing your home

Wildfires are a growing threat in Colorado and can occur year-round with little warning. The City is working hard in collaboration with Jefferson County and Arvada Fire to better prepare our community and mitigate risk. Residents can also take steps to be better prepared. [Visit the Arvada Fire website to learn about the Community Wildfire Protection Plan](https://www.arvadafireco.gov/291/Community-Wildfire-Protection-Plan).

- Harden your home: To keep your home safe from wildfires, focus on three things: stopping flames from touching your home, protecting it from heat, and blocking flying embers. The [National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) provides information](https://www.nfpa.org/en/education-and-research/wildfire/preparing-homes-for-wildfire) on how to better protect your home from wildfires.
- Create defensible space: Create defensible space around your home as a vital barrier against wildfires. This area, free from flammable materials and vegetation, significantly lowers the risk of fire reaching your property.
- Select fire-resistant plants: Incorporate fire-resistant plants in your landscaping to enhance your home's wildfire defense. These plants, less prone to ignition, add an extra layer of safety while keeping your landscape looking good.

### Preparing your family

Develop a comprehensive wildfire action plan to include evacuation routes, emergency contacts and safety procedures. Practice this plan regularly. Pack a "Go" bag for each family member, including water, food, medications and important documents.

### During a fire

- Follow all evacuation orders.
- Follow all orders from first responders.
- Do not go back into an evacuated area until approved by first responders.

### After a fire

- Stay out of all evacuated areas until the area has been reopened by first responders.
- Stay informed with the City through news releases and social media for recovery resources.

Flooding usually occurs between April and October in Arvada. Ralston Creek and the I-70 underpasses have a higher likelihood of flooding but there is risk across the city.

1. [Flood](#tab4614c9c6-6538-492c-b047-782cf8690dbc_1)

**![flooded street](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6321)**

Flooding usually occurs between April and October in Arvada. Ralston Creek and the I-70 underpasses have a higher likelihood of flooding but there is risk across the city.

**Before a flood:**

- Know your [neighborhood and workplace flood risk](https://www.arvadaco.gov/697/Floodplain-Risk)and history.
- Identify areas you would relocate to during floods which are higher in elevation and not downstream of dams.

**During a flood:**

- Follow all evacuation orders and first responders orders.
- In case of a flash flood warning, move to higher ground immediately.
- If you cannot evacuate, go to the highest floor in your house, make sure to bring supplies with you.
- Do not cross water that is above your knees.
- Do not drive across a flooded area or around barricades.
- Avoid standing water - it can become contaminated and conceal unknown risks.
- Avoid moving water - six inches can knock you off your feet.

**After a flood:**

- Wait for official messaging that the water is safe to drink.
- Throw away food and water that has been contacted by flood water.
- Have flood damages evaluated by professionals to include mold

1. [Extreme Weather](#tab63b9a224-be79-421a-a005-92419e2afa27_0)

Arvada is faced by both extreme heat and cold every year. Temperatures often drop below freezing during the winter and can peak above 100 degrees during the summer. Both extreme heat and cold can lead to injury and even death in some cases especially for higher risk individuals.**![cars covered in snow style=](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6322)**

Extreme cold

**During Extreme Cold:**

- Dress for the cold. Wear layers of loose fitting clothing.
- Try to stay dry and out of the wind.
- Wear a hat and cover your face with a mask or scarf.
- Check your household heating and water systems to ensure both have not become compromised from the extreme temperatures.
- Ensure your vehicle has a winter survival kit to include warm clothes, blankets, a shovel, and sand at a minimum.

### Extreme Heat

**During Extreme Heat:**

- Stay indoors as much as possible. If you do not have air conditioning stay on the lowest floor possible and in the shade.
- Consume water constantly, even if you are not thirsty.
- Continue to eat food regularly.
- Never leave children or pets alone in closed vehicles.
- Increase the number of breaks if conducting strenuous activities.Check on family and friends who do not have air conditioning.

1. [Cyber](#tab63b9a224-be79-421a-a005-92419e2afa27_1)

**![decorative](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6323)**

As more of our lives are located on the internet cyber attacks are becoming more and more of a threat. Cyber attacks are malicious attempts to access or damage a computer or network system. Cyber attacks can hinder the operation of major utilities, telecommunications, transportation services and more.

### Preparing yourself against Cyber attacks

- Create strong passwords or passphrases that include letters, numbers, and characters.
- Keep software systems up to date on your phone and personal computers.
- Utilize Multi-Factor Authentication whenever possible to provide another layer of security verification.
- Limit the amount of personal information you share online or over the phone.
- Do not click on links in texts or emails from people you do not know.

**During a Cyber attack:**

- Check your credit card and bank statements for unrecognized charges.
- Check your credit report for new accounts or loans you do not recognize.
- Consider turning off the device that has been affected. Take it to a professional to scan for potential viruses.
- Let work, school or other systems owners know what happened.

**After a Cyber attack:**

- Contact banks, credit card companies and other financial institutions where you hold accounts. Some accounts may need to be placed on holds if they were attacked.
- File a report with local police so there is an official record of the incident.
- Depending on what information was stolen contact the necessary agencies as needed:
  - The [Social Security Administration](https://oig.ssa.gov/report/) 800-269-0271
  - [Colorado DMV](https://dmv.colorado.gov/)
  - [The Federal Trade Commission](https://www.ftc.gov/)

## **How the City Prepares**

We coordinate with local, regional, and national partners — including FEMA, Jefferson County, Arvada Fire, and local nonprofits — to plan, train, and practice together.

- **Emergency Operations Center (EOC):** the hub for coordination during major incidents.
- **Public Communication:** timely, accurate updates across multiple platforms.
- **Recovery Planning:** strategies to restore services and support our community after a crisis.

### Local Partnerships

We partner with local, regional, state and federal agencies, along with businesses, nonprofits and community groups.

**Local Emergency Services -** Our team works closely with first responders to handle incidents as quickly as possible.

**Nonprofit Organizations -** These organizations play a vital role in providing shelter, food and medical assistance that may be needed in a large-scale emergency.

**Business Community -** Local businesses help with supplies and volunteers during the crisis. The are also vital to the economic recovery and the overall stability of Arvada during and after any emergency.

**Xcel Energy -**Xcel Energy is the electric and natural gas utility company that serves Colorado. In the event of a hazard-related power outage, Xcel provides valuable resources to help power customers prepare and stay informed about outages affecting their area. Visit the [Xcel Energy Outage Checklist webpage](https://co.my.xcelenergy.com/s/outage-safety/outage-checklist) to learn how to report an outage, view an area outage map, check the status of restoration time, and much more.

## **Get Connected, Get Involved**

Prepared communities are resilient communities.

- [**Neighbors Connected**](/482/Neighborhood-Programs) — build stronger community ties before an emergency.
- [**Community Emergency Response Team**](https://www.arvadaco.gov/684/Arvada-CERT)**(CERT)** — hands-on training for disaster response.
- [**Colorado Volunteer Mobilizer**](https://covolunteers.state.co.us/) — be notified when help is needed most.
